notes.title: Steam Deck compatibility
notes.notes:
Hey there,

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/205910/Tiny_and_Big_Grandpas_Leftovers/]Tiny & Big[/url] was reviewed for the Steam Deck, and we're happy to announce it's running pretty well (mostly).

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3330372/685befcbf5d74553666bc3f16d1a7887601f98d1.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/3330372/f17fbca1308bca94655a6de8050fd5fc2619a1e2.png[/img][/url]

The biggest hurdle is input, since this game was released way, way before Steam Input was a thing. This just means it doesn't handle Steam Deck input 100% perfectly out of the box. However, it's perfectly playable on the device with a few adjustments, and a matching input preset - each of the provided community layouts work very well! Excellent work, everyone!

Additionally, there's a bug in the native Linux version that makes the menu not register any mouse button input when run on Steam Deck. We therefore advise you to instead run the Windows build inside the magic Proton emulation layer. By the time this news is posted, that should be happening automatically after you install the game. Just in case it's not, you can set it up yourself, it's easy: go to Properites, then Compatibility. Activate the checkbox which says "Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool". You can then select the latest Proton version (we tested with Proton 7.0-4).

Everything else is going proper, so you should give it a whirl if you have one of those fancy devices laying around. Let us know what you think about the mobile Tiny & Big laser experience!

Have fun!
Black Pants

Tiny & Big, a comic styled jump and slice platformer, gives you the unique ability to shape a whole world at your will! notes.title: 64 bit Windows build is live
notes.notes:
Hey guys, we just flipped the switch to enable the 64 bit build of Tiny & Big on Windows. This hopefully means a few good things for those of you running 64 bit Windowses:
[list]
[*]Physics performance will improve on modern CPUs, we've seen frame rates go up by about 10%
[*]Less out-of-memory errors or crashes when running on integrated graphics chips
[*]The sweet, fuzzy feeling that your 64 bit hardware purchases are just a little bit more justified.
[/list]
If it doesn't work for you, especially for those of you running 32 bit Windows, please tell us in the forums. Thanks!

And one more little thing, we recently enabled Steam leaderboards for the game, so you can compare your awesome puzzle solving speed-runs. Enjoy!

Tiny & Big version 1.2
- Fixed "Invincible Fighter" achievement not being unlocked (win final boss fight without dying)
- Added support for up to 5 mouse buttons (previously 3). All buttons can be assigned in the controls menu.
- Added support for the following game controllers on Windows:
Thrustmaster Dual Analog, Logitech Dual Action, Logitech F310, Sony DualShock
- Added support for the following game controllers on Mac and Linux:
Logitech Dual Action, Logitech F310
- Fixed support for Wireless Xbox 360 controller on Mac
- Fixed support for Xbox 360 controller d-pad on Mac
- Fixed DPI scaling issues on Windows, which caused the game to be scaled larger than the actual resolution in fullscreen
- Fixed some cases where the Steam leaderboard rank wasn't shown at the end of a level
- Game no longer quits when certain files are write-protected
- Disabled warning when saving game to disk fails, but save to Steam Cloud was successful
- Added more checkpoints in 'The Horrible Moment', 'Unusual Disturbance', and 'Buried'
- Fixed texture of the yellow door
- Adjusted the volume of 'Daktari' during the final boss battle
- System requirements are checked only on first run. This avoids warnings popping up everytime the game is launched.
- Added 64 bit executable on Mac OS
- Spanish and French menu controls texts are no longer mixed up
- Fixed a few rare menu crashes

notes.title: Now Available - Tiny and Big: Grandpa's Leftovers
notes.notes:
Tiny and Big in Grandpa's Leftovers is Now Available on Steam.

Tiny & Big, a comic styled jump and slice platformer, gives you the unique ability to shape a whole world at your will! You are Tiny, a nerdy inventor who tries to reclaim his most beloved possession: Grandpa's white, fine rib underpants! On his journey through a forsaken desert he will meet mysterious creatures, no clowns, a taxi robot and his arch enemy: Big!
